summary: Assisted fast-path snapshot + surgical demotion for prefetch/quant profile incompatibility causing elevated tail latency
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sudden increase in tail latency (95p -> 2.1s) and a small but rising rate of 5xx errors after a targeted optimizer rollout that enabled KV-prefetch + quant8 profile for portions of traffic. The customer is on Dedicated capacity and observed degradation for a subset of API keys (tenant-scoped).

Impact:
- LuminaDocs production traffic seeing elevated 95th percentile latency and intermittent 5xx on text generation routes.
- Visible customer-facing slowdowns for their document-summarization webhook.
- Business impact: degraded user experience; customer requests assisted rollback and safe steps to avoid data loss or cache thrashing.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-us-east-3 (g4dn-style fleet)
- Model variants: gpt-open-13b-raw (baseline), gpt-open-13b-quant8 (new rollout)
- Traffic split: 20% to quant8 variant (tenant-gated), remainder to baseline
- Time window: degradation started ~2026-03-09 21:34 UTC

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1. Send standard generation request for doc-summarize route with seq_len ~1024 tokens.
2. Observe tail latency >1.8s and occasional 5xx (in 0.3-0.7% of requests).
3. Reverting traffic to baseline in customer canary reduces errors but latency remains variable.

Logs & telemetry pointers:
- Customer request IDs: lum-req-6721, lum-req-6724, lum-req-6730
- Trace link: https://trace.redwood.ai/trace/lumina/2026-03-09/6721
- Serving runtime dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dp-us-east-3/metrics?panel=kv_prefetch_evictions
- Error sample (snippet): HTTP 500: "kv_evict_mismatch: cache key absent during kv restore"

Requested by customer:
- Immediate assisted rollback of optimizer changes for tenant key(s).
- Guidance on safe demote (fast-path snapshot + surgical traffic demotion) to avoid cold-cache storms and QoS degradation.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:18 - Support - Ava Kim: Escalating to SRE and Runtime team. Customer requests assisted rollback; they are on Dedicated tier and have active production traffic.

2026-03-10 10:02 - SRE - Priya Nair: Noted correlation between kv-prefetch enablement and spike in KV eviction metrics. Hypothesis: quantized kernel path changes timing of KV cache lifecycle and causes mismatch on simultaneous evict/restore under certain sequence lengths.

2026-03-10 11:40 - Runtime Eng - Mateo Ruiz: Reproduced locally with synthetic traffic using seq_len 900-1100 and mixed batch sizes. Observed evict-restore race when prefetch wins but quant path delays writeback. Will prepare snapshot and demotion playbook.

2026-03-11 02:06 - Support - Ava Kim: Customer requested a minimal-impact plan: keep baseline serving while surgically demoting quant variant for only LuminaDocs keys and restore previous quant snapshot for later canary.

2026-03-11 08:45 - Assignee - Diego Morales: Drafted stepwise mitigation below; scheduling 10:00 UTC window for assisted action with customer concurrence. Linked runbook and PR for safe demote script.
investigation_notes:
Telemetry summary:
- 95p latency baseline pre-rollout: 0.74s; post-rollout peak: 2.1s.
- KV-prefetch evictions/sec spiked from 0.2 -> 7.4 for tenant on quant nodes.
- CPU utilization on quant nodes increased by ~18%; mem pressure remained constant.
- Correlated events: autoscaler briefly spawned extra nodes at 21:37 UTC but some requests hit newly provisioned nodes with empty KV, provoking restore attempts.

Hypotheses tested:
1) KV-prefetch writeback ordering race with quant kernel async flush -> reproduced with synthetic load.
2) Batch formation differences between quant and raw that expose longer critical sections -> partial reproduction.
3) Model weight layout mismatch unlikely (no model push recently).

Commands/runbook snippets tried:
- Prefetch disable toggle for tenant (dry-run): /api/v1/admin/optimizer/toggle?tenant=lumina&feature=kv_prefetch&state=off -- simulated but NOT executed in prod.
- Snapshot creation for quant8 profile: snapshot create --tenant=lumina --profile=quant8 --tag=pre-demote-20260310

Observations:
- Surgical demote (traffic only) reduced 5xx to near 0 but 95p remained elevated until KV warmup completed; warmup needed many hours for large working sets.
- Fast-path snapshot+restore allows atomic rollback of optimizer profile without full cache eviction if done per-node with node quiesce.
resolution:
Mitigation applied (2026-03-12 10:05 UTC):
1) Executed tenant-scoped 'surgical demote' using demotion tool that adjusts routing policy: moved LuminaDocs traffic away from quant8 variant to baseline (10%->0% split) with a shadow log for telemetry.
2) Created and stored a fast-path snapshot of quant8 optimizer state (tag: pre-demote-20260310) to S3-compatible snapshot store.
3) Ran per-node graceful quiesce and applied per-node profile revert for quant path; ensured kv-prefetch was disabled on nodes serving LuminaDocs while leaving cluster-wide setting unchanged.

Outcome:
- 5xx errors returned to baseline (<0.05%).
- 95p latency reduced to ~0.82s within 3 hours as KV warmed; customer confirmed improved UX.

Follow-up actions and recommendations:
- Backfill: schedule a controlled canary for quant8 with smaller 1% traffic split and explicit KV warmup routine (background cache populate) before increasing traffic.
- Add a safeguard to demotion runbook: require 'fast-path snapshot' creation and per-node quiesce for any tenant-scoped optimizer change.
- Add metric alert: if KV-prefetch evictions/sec > 3 for sustained 5m during a rollout, auto-demote that tenant variant and open an incident.
- Engineering follow-up: add an ordering fence in the quant kernel path to avoid writeback/read race; tracking in ENG-RTX-2043.

Resolution status: Customer confirmed mitigation and requested Support assistance to coordinate the canary (scheduled 2026-03-15).
next_steps: Coordinate with LuminaDocs to run 1% controlled canary on 2026-03-15. Runtime eng (Mateo) to be present.
Add the fast-path snapshot requirement to the optimizer rollout checklist in Confluence.
Implement automated demote circuit breaker for sustained KV-prefetch evictions (ENG ticket ENG-RTX-2043).
